_comment: SDG&E Schedule TOU-DR1 — Residential Time of Use Service.
Total Electric Rate ($/kWh), transcribed from the utility's own tariff table.
This file exists so the numbers carry their citation. Rates were previously
two constants in energy_model.py with the note 'approximate SDG&E TOU-DR1' —
and they were about 40% low and missing an entire pricing tier.
TO UPDATE: SDG&E republishes this table on each rate change. Download the
current 'Schedule TOU-DR1 Total Rates Table' PDF, transcribe the Total
Electric Rate column, and bump effective_date. Do not interpolate or round.
source_note: Total Electric Rate column (UDC + EECC + WF-NBC/DWR-BC), bundled residential customer.

summer._comment: June 1 - October 31. October is SUMMER, which is easy to get wrong.

_comment: Hours are the same year-round; only the PRICE changes by season.
On-Peak 4-9 PM every day. Super Off-Peak differs weekday vs weekend.
The weekday 10:00-14:00 super-off-peak block was previously March/April
only and is now year-round — see periods_source_url.
The base services charge is a fixed daily charge and is NOT used in waste
arithmetic: turning a light off does not change it, so including it would
overstate every saving. Recorded here because it is part of the tariff and
someone will ask why the modelled bill is lower than a real one.
The baseline credit applies to usage up to 130% of baseline allowance and

season_month_boundaries: The rate table is split into Summer and Winter blocks but does not print
the date ranges, so the boundaries here come from secondary sources —
consistently reported as summer June 1 - October 31, winter November 1 -
May 31. This is the one value in this file not read off an SDG&E rate
document. It changes only WHICH column applies, never a rate.
An earlier revision had summer as June-September, which billed all of
OCTOBER at winter rates: $0.62200 instead of $0.69654 on-peak, a 12%
understatement for a whole month. October being summer is the easy thing
